videos.title: Vietnam Veterans Memorial Ceremony
videos.description: The Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., hosts an observance ceremony for veterans of that war.

videos.title: C-SPAN Interviews the Blue Angels
videos.description: C-SPAN interviews the U.S. Navy Blue Angels team on what life is like flying for the iconic squadron and what it takes to become a member; this interview takes place during the 2026 San Francisco Fleet Week.

videos.title: Veterans Day Concert at the National Cathedral
videos.description: The President's Own United States Marine Band performs a concert at the National Cathedral in honor of Veterans Day.

videos.title: American Military Cemeteries Around the World
videos.description: Learn the history of American military cemeteries around the world, courtesy of the American Battle Monuments Commission.

videos.title: Oral Histories
videos.description: U.S. Navy veteran Harlan Twible recounts being a young officer on the USS Indianapolis after it was sunk in shark-infested waters by two Japanese torpedoes.

videos.title: The Battleship Missouri Veterans Day Ceremony
videos.description: The Battleship Missouri Memorial at Pearl Harbor hosts a ceremony honoring military veterans in Honolulu, Hawaii.

videos.title: Lectures in History
videos.description: When Kentucky became a state in 1792, it had a choice: keep slavery or abolish it. University of Kentucky professor Melanie Goan teaches a class on the state's relationship with the institution of slavery until the 1863 Emancipation Proclamation.

videos.title: America 250
videos.description: Historian and former Harvard University president Drew Gilpin Faust reflects on the life and legacy of President James Buchanan. Her essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned to help mark America's 250th birthday this year.

videos.title: The Mathew Brady Story and the Clara Barton Story
videos.description: This 1961 U.S. Army film tells the stories about both famed Civil War photographer Mathew Brady and Clara Barton, founder of the American Red Cross in 1881.

videos.title: The Presidency
videos.description: Historian Diana Carlin analyzes the life of Julia Grant using the first lady's memoirs. The Ulysses S. Grant Historic Site hosts this event.

videos.title: C-SPAN Visits the Golden Spike National Historic Site
videos.description: C-SPAN visits the Golden Spike Site at Promontory, Utah, where the Central Pacific and Union Pacific railroads joined to mark the completion of the first transcontinental railroad on May 10, 1869.

videos.title: America 250
videos.description: Harvard University history professor Annette Gordon-Reed reflects on the life and legacy of President Andrew Johnson. Her essay is part of a project called In Pursuit, commissioned to help mark America's 250th birthday in 2026.

videos.title: America 250
videos.description: Historians explore the ideas that sparked the American Revolution, as well as the key personalities and enduring impact of the Revolutionary Era. The event is organized by the Jack Miller Center and The American Revolution Institute.

videos.title: The Civil War
videos.description: Author Jonathan Jones discusses America's first opioid epidemic, which comprised veterans taking opium and morphine to ease distress after the Civil War.

videos.title: Reel America
videos.description: This 1944 documentary, which was intended to encourage African Americans to enlist in the U.S. Army during World War II, traces the history of African-American contributions to society during war and peace.
